title: An amount written as a percentage is judged right or wrong on three kinds
body:
## Summary
check() treats a percent-sign answer as unsure on every amount kind except a fraction of an amount, a missing number and a computation in a unit, where 2400% is right for 24 kg and 24% is wrong.

## Description
The rule "an amount is never a percentage, the desk does not guess" was written as two hand lists in desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts check (pct kinds at desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2211, rate/area/stat/pyth/pyth-dp at desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2216) and once in checkRatio for a missing ratio term (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2068). The fractions kinds were never added: "Find 3/5 of 40 kg" took 2400% as RIGHT and 24% as WRONG, and "3/4 = ?/12" took 900% as right while "2:3 = ?:15" took 1000% as unsure. That breaks the file's own stance "unsure is never wrong" (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:28) and prints a wrong ring for the right number. Fixed: the amount list now holds `of`, `missing` and a `compute` with a unit; a bare computation keeps taking any equal form (75% for 3/4). Judged on the repo's own stance (no registry technique governs a maths judge's accepted forms).

## Flow
- learner types 24% for "Find 3/5 of 40 kg" -> check() -> no amount rule for kind `of` -> slips miss -> verdict wrong, TV rings a right number
- fix: extend the amount predicate in check() to `of`, `missing` and `compute` with a unit; pin with a table test over all three kinds

## Expected impact
A learner who writes a percent sign on an amount is asked, never ringed or ticked on a guess; measured by the school-rules table. Could break: a bare computation answered as a percent if the unit test were wrong - pinned (75% for 3/4 stays right).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no right or wrong verdict on a percent-sign amount
Before: 9 percent writings over fraction-of, missing and unit compute -> 5 right, 4 wrong, 0 unsure
After: 9/9 unsure; amount writings, a bare 75% and workedAnswer unchanged
Method: gate - a school-rules-test table went red (2400% right), then green on the change
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
probe before: check({shape:"fraction-of",expr:"3/5 of 40",unit:"kg"},"2400%") -> right; "24%" -> wrong; check({shape:"missing",expr:"3/4 = ?/12"},"900%") -> right; check({shape:"ratio",expr:"2:3 = ?:15"},"1000%") -> unsure
desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2216 (the amount predicate after the fix)
tools/school-rules-test.cjs (test "an amount, a missing number or a unit answer written as a percentage is unsure")

title: A fault reading the spec let leaksSchool pass the hint unchecked
body:
## Summary
leaksSchool returned false (no leak) when read(spec) threw, while its header and its other catch refuse the line on a fault.

## Description
leaksSchool has two fault doors: the read of the spec (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2670) and the check body (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2770). The header says an internal fault refuses the line, the strict side; the body did, the read returned false, so any defect in read() would let a model's hint through to the TV unchecked - "could not check" spelled as "no leak" (error-handling/error-doors, _laws failure-not-empty-success). Fixed: the read fault returns true; a malformed spec (read ok:false) still has nothing to leak.

## Flow
- a spec whose reading throws (any defect in structure/readKind) -> leaksSchool -> catch -> false -> hint shown
- fix: return true in the read catch, keep checkerFault; test with a throwing-getter spec

## Expected impact
Withholding holds under a checker defect; the operator still sees the checkerFault line. Could break: nothing on a readable spec (suites unchanged).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every leak-check fault fails closed
Before: 1 of 2 fault doors fails open (throwing spec -> false)
After: 2 of 2 fail closed (true); malformed spec and empty line still false
Method: gate - school-rules-test red (actual false) then green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2670 (was: checkerFault("school.leaksSchool read", e); return false;)
desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2770 (body catch returns true)

title: paper-draft-test ran in no gate
body:
## Summary
tools/paper-draft-test.cjs, the only suite for desk/src/lib/rules/paperDraft.ts, was not in desk/package.json rulesSuites nor in any workflow.

## Description
The phone keeps a typed paper across a reload through draftKey, serialiseDraft and parseDraft (desk/src/lib/rules/paperDraft.ts:11-33). Its suite existed and was green by hand (UAT recertify notes cite 4/0) but no gate ran it, so a parser regression would merge green (test-harness/out-of-graph-artifacts). Every other suite in this context is wired. Fixed: added to rulesSuites before harness-rules-test (shared-surface lock).

## Flow
- grep "paper-draft-test" desk/package.json .github -> 0 hits
- fix: insert into rulesSuites; run-rules --list on the suite alone

## Expected impact
The draft parser is held by the merge gate. Could break: nothing; 4 tests, 89 ms.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every suite of the context runs in the gate
Before: 0 gates run paper-draft-test
After: 1 (rulesSuites); run-rules green 4/0; list unique, harness-rules-test last
Method: gate - run-rules --list on the suite exit 0; list integrity check exit 0
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
for f in tools/*-test.cjs: NOT WIRED: paper-draft-test.cjs (the only one of this context)
desk/package.json rulesSuites (after: "paper-draft-test.cjs" before "harness-rules-test.cjs")

title: storyOf and topFormOf swallowed checker faults; workedAnswer had no door
body:
## Summary
Two catch sites in school.ts returned null with no checkerFault, and the exported workedAnswer let a fault escape to its caller.

## Description
rules/fault.ts says a throw that is not Unreadable is a desk defect the operator learns of through checkerFault; 12 school.ts catches route there. storyOf (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:3075) and topFormOf (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:3842) used a bare catch returning null, so a defect read as "no story"/"no top form" and steered a set (desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:514-577) silently; workedAnswer (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:4594) read without a try, so a fault reached desk/src/lib/desk/worked.ts:34. The error-doors ratchet does not count them (their bodies return a value). error-handling/swallowed-error-prevention.

## Flow
- a spec whose structure throws -> storyOf -> null, no log; workedAnswer -> throws
- fix: checkerFault in both catches; guard workedAnswer's read and return null

## Expected impact
A checker defect behind a step-up set or a worked example reaches the log once. Could break: nothing on readable specs.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every checker fault in school.ts reaches the log
Before: 2 silent catches + 1 unguarded export (workedAnswer threw TypeError)
After: 0; all three return null and log "[rules] checker fault in school.<site>"
Method: gate - school-rules-test red (TypeError escaped) then green; error-doors-test 0
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -n "catch" desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts before: 3064 `} catch {`, 3831 `} catch {` (no checkerFault); workedAnswer `const r = read(spec);` unguarded

title: The comma-system list was copied into school.ts and kinds.ts
body:
## Summary
workedAnswer and kinds.ts commaValue re-spelled `=== "cz" || === "de"` instead of asking taskText commaSystem.

## Description
commaSystem (desk/src/lib/rules/taskText.ts:56) is the one authority on which systems write a decimal comma (_laws one-authority-per-vocabulary); school.ts used it for printing and money but copied the list in workedAnswer, and kinds.ts commaValue copied it for linear answers. A third comma system would be read and printed but written with a point in a worked answer and left unread in a typed linear answer. Fixed both; a comment-stripped source scan with a canary pins it.

## Flow
- grep the inline list in desk/src: 5 sites, 2 in this context (school.ts workedAnswer, kinds.ts:89)
- fix: call commaSystem; add the scan test

## Expected impact
One edit adds a comma system everywhere in this context. Could break: nothing (same two systems).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one authority for the comma systems
Before: 2 inline copies in this context
After: 0 (scan test); workedAnswer 7,15 in cz, 7.15 in uk unchanged
Method: gate - scan test red on school.ts, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/lib/rules/kinds.ts:89 (before) `(system === "cz" || system === "de") && /^-?\d+,\d+$/`
desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts workedAnswer `const comma = system === "cz" || system === "de";`

title: school.ts contract docs named half the shapes and a stale currency claim
body:
## Summary
Two orphaned JSDoc blocks, a wellFormed doc naming 7 of 13 shapes, a unitOf doc naming 4 of 13, and REJECT.rateUnit claiming a cost is only euros or pounds.

## Description
STAT_RE's description sat above PROB_COLOURS and SchoolSlip's field note above its own doc block (back-to-back JSDoc, the first attaches to nothing); the exported wellFormed contract (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:1290) and unitOf (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:4471) stopped at W7 batch 3; REJECT.rateUnit (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:585) said "euros or pounds" while readKind accepts Kč since MB-B4 (isMoney) - a stale capability claim (copy-auditor). Fixed all four; the reason table that pinned the old sentence now pins the new one and a test forbids the old.

## Flow
- probe: count back-to-back JSDoc, shapes named in each doc, crowns in rateUnit
- fix: move/merge the blocks, extend both docs, reword rateUnit

## Expected impact
A reader of the exported contracts sees every shape. Could break: nothing at runtime (one reason string).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - docs say what the code takes
Before: orphaned 2; wellFormed 7/13; unitOf 4/13; rateUnit names crowns: no
After: 0; 12/13; 11/13 (compute described in the lead); yes
Method: gate - the unit-rate reason table went red on the copy change and was strengthened; doc counts by probe
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A spoken answer of a hundred or more in English was never heard
body:
## Summary
figuresOfEnglish, the reader saidIn hears a spoken answer through, stopped at ninety-nine, while the Czech reader and the leak reader read hundreds.

## Description
Three number-word readers carry one rule: school.ts wordsToDigits reads "a hundred", "three hundred and five", "thousand" (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2341-2369); figuresOfCzech reads "sto dvacet jedna" (desk/src/lib/rules/numberWords.ts:75); figuresOfEnglish (desk/src/lib/rules/numberWords.ts:105) had no hundred or thousand, so saidIn (desk/src/lib/rules/saidValue.ts:55) refused "I got one hundred and eighty" for 180 and the explanation could never settle an item whose answer is 100 or more (a fraction of 300, an area, a percent change) - in English only. Fixed with a cardinal reader up to 999 999 inside figuresOfEnglish; EN_CARD is untouched, so the leak reader is unchanged.

## Flow
- learner explains by voice "I got one hundred and eighty" -> saidIn("180") -> figures "1 hundred and 80" -> runs [1,80] -> not heard -> item stays unsure
- fix: hundreds and thousands in figuresOfEnglish; table + saidIn tests, closed cases kept

## Expected impact
An English learner's spoken three-digit answer settles as a Czech one does. Could break: a transcript's figures read differently - pinned (18, 108, 30 still not heard).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a spoken value of 100+ is heard in English
Before: saidIn true for 0/4 English answers >= 100 (180, 120, 2400, 300); Czech 121 true
After: 4/4; 18, 108, 30 against the same transcripts still false
Method: gate - school-rules-test red (figures "1 hundred and 80") then green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe before: saidIn("180","I got one hundred and eighty") false; figuresOfEnglish -> "I got 1 hundred and 80"; saidIn("121","vyšlo mi sto dvacet jedna") true

title: The Paper draft survives Send, so a reload restores and re-sends a sent paper
body:
## Summary
PaperPanel posts paper.enter and leaves the rows and the stored draft, so after a reload the phone restores the rows that were already sent.

## Description
paperDraft.ts keeps the typed rows per learner (desk/src/lib/rules/paperDraft.ts:11-33); the page writes on every edit and restores on load (desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:507-520). Send (desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:70) never clears it - noted, not filed, in uat/runs/2026-10-09-maths-l1 recertify evidence. A learner who sends, reloads and sends again enters the paper twice. The fix belongs in the phone page (another context): clear the draft key and the rows on a successful paper.enter. Out of this round's paths.

## Flow
- type a paper -> Send -> reload the phone -> the same rows are back -> Send again
- fix: on a 2xx paper.enter, localStorage.removeItem(draftKey(id)) and setPaperRows([blankRow()])

## Expected impact
A sent paper is not offered again; measured by the instrument. Could break: a failed send must keep the draft (send result checked).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a sent paper is not restored
Before: by reading: 0 clears of the draft key after Send (PaperPanel.tsx:70, page.tsx:507-520)
After: not measured
Method: simulation - the fix is in desk/src/app/phone (another context); walked: send+reload restores rows
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:70 onClick={() => void post({ type: "paper.enter", rows: rawOf(rows), ... })}
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:515 editPaperRows = ... keepDraft(...)  (no clear on send)
instrument: a phone-panel-test case: seat a learner, edit rows (keepDraft writes desk.paperDraft.<id>), post paper.enter green, then assert the storage key is removed and a remount restores one blank row; plus a store test of two identical paper.enter posts

title: One school-stretch test takes 25.5 s of the suite's 26.2 s
body:
## Summary
Test 2 of tools/school-stretch-test.cjs runs 84 practice-route set writes at about 300 ms each; the generators themselves take 0.13 ms a spec.

## Description
tools/school-stretch-test.cjs:112-142 walks every unit x three learners x usual and step-up through makeItems (the route path with the store), 25 517 ms of a 26 235 ms suite in this run; school-toprung (16.5 s) is property sweeps by design. The generator cost is measured at 0.13 ms/spec and 0.24 ms/top-rung spec, so the time is in the route path, not the rules. Every PR pays it in quality.yml.

## Flow
- node ../tools/school-stretch-test.cjs -> test 2 25 517 ms
- instrument the 84 calls; keep the per-unit assertion, move the full matrix to the pure makeSchoolItems where the store adds nothing

## Expected impact
A faster desk gate. Could break: coverage of the route path if over-narrowed (one route call per unit kept).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - gate time
Before: test 2 25 517 ms / suite 26 235 ms
After: not measured
Method: simulation - the split of the 300 ms per call is not yet measured; the instrument is named
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: school-stretch run: "✔ 2: a step-up set is strictly harder ... (25517.568ms)", duration_ms 26234.99; probe: gen per spec 0.126 ms, top 0.240 ms
instrument: time each makeItems call in tools/school-stretch-test.cjs test 2 (84 calls), split store write vs generator vs fair(); then the same figure after caching or narrowing the per-unit loop

title: school.ts parses one decimal text six ways and keeps two of several readers
body:
## Summary
The "w.f" text to exact rational step is written six times, GAP_SRC and RGAP_SRC are one pattern, readCombined and readMixed carry the same instruction-tail regex, and writings() repeats writingsOf/plainText.

## Description
Copies: desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:507, :686 (sideQ), :736 (pctQ), :930, :999, :1008; GAP_SRC :4014 = RGAP_SRC :4158; the tail regex at :3929 and :3957; writings :4563 vs writingsOf :2260 / plainText :2253. Each pair can drift (a fix to one reader of "Give your answer as a decimal" misses the other). Not the open unit-split card: this is helper consolidation inside the file, and it should ride with that split.

## Flow
- grep the copies (above)
- fold to one decQ, one GAP, one tail, one writings; rerun the four suites

## Expected impact
One place per parsing rule. Could break: a reader's exact accepted text - the read-back tests pin every printed question.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation per parsing rule
Before: 6 + 2 + 2 + 2 copies
After: not measured
Method: simulation - overlaps the open Lane B split of school.ts; building it now would conflict
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: count of copies (decimal-text->Q, GAP/RGAP, the instruction tail, writings vs writingsOf) before and after, with school-rules, school-practice, school-toprung and gcse-units green; land with or after the open unit-split card to avoid a conflict

title: Which answer kinds take a percent form is a hand list a new kind can skip
body:
## Summary
check() decides the percent form by OR-chains over kind names (two lists, plus checkRatio and convert), so a 20th kind silently takes 2400% as right - the defect just fixed for three kinds.

## Description
desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2211 and :2216 enumerate 11 of the 19 Kind members by hand; the rest fall through to "any equal form is right". marks.ts already pins its vocabulary as a total list that fails to compile when a member is missing (desk/src/lib/rules/marks.ts:203-206). A Record keyed by Kind["k"] makes the next kind a compile error (§4.7: the list is not derived from the ground truth).

## Flow
- add a Kind member (a new unit) -> check() -> no amount entry -> percent accepted
- fix: a total table keyed by Kind["k"]; the compiler lists the missing member

## Expected impact
The next unit cannot reopen this hole. Could break: nothing if the table reproduces today's choices (the percent table tests pin them).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a new kind must declare its percent rule
Before: 11 of 19 kinds named; a seeded kind compiles silently
After: not measured
Method: simulation - the refactor is S but rewrites the branch just fixed; separated so the fix lands alone
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2216 const amount = K.k === "rate" || K.k === "area" || ... || (K.k === "compute" && unit !== undefined);
instrument: a total Record<Kind["k"], "any" | "amount" | "percent-amount" | "own"> in check(); seed a new Kind member and watch tsc --noEmit go red, then the school-rules percent table stays green

title: A missing number written as a percentage is told the question asks for an amount
body:
## Summary
Since 6acd2750 a percent answer to "3/4 = ?/12" is unsure with WHY.amountAsPercent, which says the question asks for an amount; it asks for a missing number.

## Description
WHY.amountAsPercent (desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:1969) serves every amount kind; a missing number and a missing ratio term (checkRatio, desk/src/lib/rules/school.ts:2068) are counts, and the TV says this sentence (kinds.ts unsureLine -> NOT_SURE(n, why)). One more WHY sentence for the two missing kinds keeps the words true.

## Flow
- type 900% for 3/4 = ?/12 -> unsure -> "the question asks for an amount"
- fix: WHY.numberAsPercent for missing and ratio-missing

## Expected impact
The caption names what was asked. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the unsure line says what was asked
Before: 2 kinds (missing, ratio-missing) get the amount sentence
After: not measured
Method: simulation - copy choice for the owner's voice; the instrument is a rows test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: check({shape:"missing",expr:"3/4 = ?/12"},"900%","uk").why === "This is written as a percentage; the question asks for an amount, and the desk does not guess."
instrument: a rows test of the unsure sentence per kind: missing and ratio-missing say "the missing number", amounts say "an amount"

title: hint.ts keeps its own copy of the comma-system list
body:

Claim: quality - one authority
Before: 1 copy in desk/src/lib/desk
After: not measured
Method: simulation - out of this round's paths
Result: better
